messages.bounded_file: Keep workspace/slurm/gpu_job.slurm.txt as a regular UTF-8 practice file smaller than 100000 bytes; do not execute it.
messages.header_layout: Put every #SBATCH directive before the first shell command; use one unquoted long option and one literal value per line (for example #SBATCH --time=00:10:00).
messages.unique_directives: Keep each #SBATCH option only once. Inspect both repeated lines and keep the intended value; do not rely on their order.
messages.supported_options: Use only the options shown in this fictional exercise, plus optional --nodes=1 and --ntasks=1. Remove extra resource options or short aliases; this bounded review is not a general Slurm validator.
messages.single_allocation: Use at most one node and one Slurm task per job: omit --nodes/--ntasks or set each to exactly 1. The array cap limits array jobs, not the number of Slurm tasks inside each job.
messages.account: Use --account=es_fuge in the fictional review file.
messages.gpu_model: Request exactly one explicit supported GPU: rtx_4090:1, rtx_3090:1 or pro_6000:1; special hardware still needs a separate compatibility review.
messages.no_partition: Remove the forced --partition from the practice request.
messages.cpu_limit: Use ASCII digits for --cpus-per-task, with a value from 1 to 16; remove signs such as +.
messages.memory_limit: Use a positive integer G value for --mem-per-cpu, with CPUs times GiB at most 64; remove --mem. System RAM is separate from GPU memory.
messages.time_limit: Use a positive HH:MM:SS time, at most 04:00:00, with minutes and seconds below 60.
messages.output_log: Include both %x and %j in --output so the fictional log identifies its job.
messages.error_log: Include both %x and %j in --error so the fictional error log identifies its job.

messages.bounded_file: Keep workspace/slurm/array_job.slurm.txt as a regular UTF-8 practice file smaller than 100000 bytes; do not execute it.
messages.header_layout: Put every #SBATCH directive before the first shell command; use one unquoted long option and one literal value per line (for example #SBATCH --time=00:10:00).
messages.unique_directives: Keep each #SBATCH option only once. Inspect both repeated lines and keep the intended value; do not rely on their order.
messages.supported_options: Use only the options shown in this fictional exercise, plus optional --nodes=1 and --ntasks=1. Remove extra resource options or short aliases; this bounded review is not a general Slurm validator.
messages.single_allocation: Use at most one node and one Slurm task per job: omit --nodes/--ntasks or set each to exactly 1. The array cap limits array jobs, not the number of Slurm tasks inside each job.
messages.output_unique: Include both %A and %a in --output so each array job has its own log.
messages.error_unique: Include both %A and %a in --error so each array job has its own error log.
messages.safe_resources: Keep --time=00:10:00, --cpus-per-task=1 and --mem-per-cpu=1G for the guided file repair.
